# v3.08-dev

Housekeeping release. Nothing changes on screen — this one tightens a safety net
and writes down two design decisions that had started to look like mistakes.

## Improved

- **The check that guarantees every API endpoint asks who is calling is now
  stricter.** The public API has a master on/off switch, and that switch was
  being accepted by our automated check as though it were an identity check. It
  isn't — it only answers "is this feature turned on". No endpoint was ever
  affected, and the public API has always required a valid key; the gap was in
  the safety net itself, where a future read-only endpoint could have passed the
  check while asking for no credentials at all. The check now refuses it, and
  carries its own self-tests so the allowance cannot quietly come back.

- **Company scoping now fails safe in four shared reporting queries.** If a
  caller is scoped to *no* companies, these now return nothing, which is what
  was intended. Previously that specific case could have been read as "no
  restriction". Nothing in the app could reach it — every screen and API route
  already stops earlier — so no report or export has ever shown the wrong data.
  This removes the possibility for anything added later.

## Documented

- **Two long-standing decisions are now recorded in the code**, so they read as
  deliberate rather than accidental: the country/region reference list is shared
  across the whole instance on purpose (it holds no customer data, and filtering
  it would hide geographies you are meant to be able to plan against), and the
  partner-program catalogue is intentionally not filtered per company, because
  programs are instance-wide configuration rather than customer data.

- **Two corrections to the contributor documentation**: the note describing how
  release pull requests are opened now matches what actually happens, and the
  command used to gather notes for a stable release no longer mis-selects which
  pre-releases belong in the list.
